text: dsh-task-worktree 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Git 任务 worktree 插件：它在仓库内为任务创建独立分支和 checkout，并用持久清单记录状态。可从模型工具或 /worktree 命令创建、列出和查看 worktree，也能把主工作区未提交改动带入；用户还可直接提交分支、合并改动回主工作区或清理 checkout。空白会话可选择 worktree 模式并设置分支名，设置页可指定新会话默认模式；会话栏显示分支标记。适合需要并行隔离 DSH 编码任务、保留会话间工作并由用户控制收尾的场景。需要 Git 2.31+ 与 Node 20+。

dsh-task-worktree adds isolated Git worktrees to DSH. Each task gets a branch and checkout in a manifest. Tools and /worktree commands manage them; users can carry changes, commit, merge back, or remove a checkout. Blank sessions can start in worktree mode. Requires Git 2.31+ and Node 20+.

dsh-task-worktree 的功能「create」：worktree_create 可按名称和可选起始提交创建任务 checkout，名称同时作为分支名；也可选择复制主工作区未提交改动。
dsh-task-worktree 的功能「list-status」：worktree_list 与 worktree_status 展示受管理 checkout 的路径、分支、状态、HEAD 和 dirty 情况，便于检查任务进度。
dsh-task-worktree 的功能「mode」：空白会话可从输入区选择 worktree 模式并填写可选名称；首条用户消息触发创建指令，设置页可配置新会话默认模式。
dsh-task-worktree 的功能「finish-merge」：用户可用 /worktree finish 将任务 checkout 的改动提交到其分支，或用 bring-back 在主工作区干净时合并回去。
dsh-task-worktree 的功能「cleanup」：/worktree remove 可删除 checkout 与分支，prune 可清理已不存在 checkout 的清单记录；当前会话所在 worktree 不允许直接删除。
希望每个任务有自己的分支和长期保存的工作副本，重启会话后还能继续。

**Complete Git worktree support for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).**

dsh-task-worktree README · dsh-task-worktree：A community plugin that gives DSH the **task-scoped worktree workflow** of Qoder / Codex / Claude Code: each task gets its own isolated `git worktree` checkout on its own branch, recorded in a per-repo manifest so it **survives sessions and restarts**. The main workspace stays untouched; conversations that use a worktree are marked with a **branch badge** on the session header (no workspace entry is created), and the changes can be **brought back** (Move to local) or **committed directly** on the worktree branch — always under explicit human control.

dsh-task-worktree README · dsh-task-worktree：It follows the design of Qoder's `Worktree` execution environment, Codex's `codex worktree create --permanent`, and Claude Code's `--worktree` sessions, adapted to DSH's session/workspace model.

dsh-task-worktree README · Design：| Concept (this plugin) | Qoder | Codex | Claude Code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Task-scoped isolated checkout | Worktree execution environment | `codex worktree create --permanent` | `claude --worktree <name>` |
| Worktrees live in `<repo>/.dsh-worktrees/` | background worktree checkout | `.codex/worktrees/` | `.claude/worktrees/` |
| Durable registry survives restarts | per-session | global index | session binding |
| Own branch per task | branch selector | — | `worktree-<name>` |
| Open as a DSH workspace from the GUI | panel selector | `codex worktree open` | launches into the worktree |
| Mark the conversation using the worktree | session badge | — | — |
| Bring changes back to main | Move to local | — | exit/cleanup prompt |
| Direct commit on the worktree branch | Review & commit panel | commit in the worktree session | commit in the worktree |
| Carry uncommitted main changes in | Include uncommitted changes toggle | — | `.worktreeinclude` |
| Auto-ignore the worktree directory | — | — | `.gitignore` tip |

   **Settings → Plugins → Task worktree** and every new conversation starts
   that way (see [Settings](#settings)).
2. **Send your first message** — the host injects one `instructions` context

dsh-task-worktree README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-task-worktree
```

Requires: DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1`+, Git 2.31+, Node 20+.

dsh-task-worktree README · Settings：The plugin declares a volatile `Config`; DeepSeek Harness turns it into a
settings form served under this plugin's profile entry id, `dsh-task-worktree`.
The card lives on the sidebar **Plugins → dsh-task-worktree** page (bundled
plugin configuration); the settings service's auto-generated page is suppressed
so the fields have exactly one surface.

dsh-task-worktree README · Settings：One setting — the mode a new conversation starts in — with three choices (they
are exactly the three states there are; a mode plus a separate "remember"
switch would describe a fourth one that means nothing):

dsh-task-worktree README · Settings：| Choice in the panel | Stored in `dsh-task-worktree` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local mode | `defaultMode: local`, `rememberLastChoice: false` | Every new conversation starts in the main workspace. |
| Worktree mode | `defaultMode: worktree`, `rememberLastChoice: false` | Every new conversation is isolated: the host injects the worktree-creation instruction with the first genuine message, no selector trip needed. |
| Remember the last choice | `rememberLastChoice: true` | The mode you picked last above the composer wins; `defaultMode` holds that pick. |

dsh-task-worktree README · Settings：The default is **Local mode**. An installation that never opens the card keeps
behaving exactly as it did before this setting existed: new conversations start
in the main workspace, and a pick in the composer selector applies to its own
conversation only.

The chosen mode applies to conversations that start empty. Picking **Local mode**
in the composer selector is an explicit answer for that conversation: the host
does not auto-arm it, whatever the setting says.

dsh-task-worktree README · Settings：The values live in this plugin's profile patch entry, so they can also be set by
hand and take effect live:

```yaml
- id: dsh-task-worktree
  config:
    defaultMode: worktree
    rememberLastChoice: false

On a host without the settings service the plugin keeps working with the
composed defaults (local mode), and the card simply does not appear.

dsh-task-worktree README · Model tools：| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `worktree_create {name, baseCommit?, includeUncommitted?}` | Create a task worktree (name = branch and relative path, slashes allowed); optionally carry uncommitted main-workspace changes in |
| `worktree_list` | List the repository's managed worktrees (state / dirty / branch) |
| `worktree_status {name?}` | Status of one worktree, or the one the current session is inside |
dsh-task-worktree README · Model tools：Delivery and cleanup actions (finish / bring-back / remove) stay **human-only** — the model never reaches them.

dsh-task-worktree README · Human commands：```
/worktree mode-on [<name>]     arm worktree mode (injection with the next message)
/worktree mode-off             disarm worktree mode
/worktree create <name> [<base>] [--carry]
/worktree list

dsh-task-worktree README · Safety model：- `@deepseek-ai/*` are **peerDependencies only** — the host supplies them; the plugin never installs infrastructure copies into a profile (a second instance breaks `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER`'s unique symbol and kills tool calls).
- `bring-back` requires a clean main workspace (`MAIN_DIRTY`) and refuses to run from inside the worktree.
- `remove` refuses the worktree the current session is working inside (`IN_USE`).
- All git operations go through `ctx.subprocess` (harness-managed); the test path uses a child_process runner.
- Manifest writes are atomic (tmp + rename); `prune` drops records whose checkout no longer exists.

dsh-task-worktree README · Local development：```bash
npm test              # smoke (worktree lifecycle) + host half + browser prefs
npm run typecheck     # client TypeScript
npm run build:client  # rebuild client/client.js (tsdown + lightningcss)
npm pack --dry-run    # inspect the tarball before publishing

dsh-task-worktree README · Local development：The suites: `test/smoke.mjs` (git lifecycle on a scratch repository),
`test/host.mjs` (the real `apply()` on a fake cordis context: settings config
and page policy, arming policy, injection), `test/prefs.mjs` (the browser preference
store; needs Node 22.6+ and skips itself on older runtimes).
